records.gloss: A psalm, a song for the day of the Sabbath.
pieces: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.

L.1: A psalm. A song for the day of the Sabbath.

R.1: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: for the Sabbath: sung on the seventh day
decisions.reason: This is the only psalm whose Hebrew title names a day. The Mishnah (Tamid 7:4) lists a psalm the Levites sang in the temple for each day of the week, with this one for the Sabbath. The psalm praises God's works (verses 5-6), fitting the day that remembers creation (Exodus 20:11).

decisions.choice: a psalm, a song
decisions.reason: Both words name a song: mizmor is a song with music (3:1), shir is the ordinary word for a song (46:1).

records.heading: It is good to give thanks

records.source: ט֗וֹב לְהֹד֥וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה וּלְזַמֵּ֖ר לְשִׁמְךָ֣ עֶלְיֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Good [it is] to give thanks to YHWH, and to sing praises to your name, Most High,
pieces: It is a good thing to thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q to sing and play in praise of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, Most High,

L.2: [It is] good to give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and to sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, Most High,

R.2: It is good to thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It is good to sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the God who is above all.

decisions.choice: sing praises: sing with music
decisions.reason: The verb (zamar) means to sing and play in praise (7:18), the root of mizmor, "psalm" (verse 1).

decisions.choice: your name, Most High: from speaking about God to speaking to him
decisions.reason: The first line speaks of the LORD; the second turns to address him. The sentence runs on to verse 4, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: the God who is above all
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title ('Elyon) means: God above everything.

records.gloss: to declare in the morning your loyal love, and your faithfulness in the nights,
pieces: to tell of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love at sunrise \q and of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness through the nights,

L.3: to declare in the morning {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness in the nights,

R.3: It is good to tell about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love every morning, \q and about how faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are every night.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: morning and nights: all the time
decisions.reason: Naming the two ends of the day means praise at every hour (55:18).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

decisions.choice: It is good
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and repeats the opening words of verse 2.

records.gloss: on [the] ten and on [the] harp, on [the] melody with [the] lyre.
pieces: with the ten-stringed instrument and the harp, \q to the sounding music of the lyre.

L.4: on [the instrument of] ten [strings] and on [the] harp, \q with [the] melody on [the] lyre.

R.4: It is good to do this with music on harps and lyres, \q and on instruments with ten strings.

decisions.choice: ten-stringed instrument, harp, lyre
decisions.reason: The kinnor was a hand-held lyre and the nevel a larger stringed instrument (33:2); the "ten" ('asor) is an instrument with ten strings, or a ten-stringed harp, as in 33:2 and 144:9.

decisions.choice: melody: a resounding sound
decisions.reason: The word (higgayon) is the one left as "Higgaion" in 9:17; here it is the sound of the lyre.

decisions.choice: It is good to do this
decisions.reason: Readable makes the verse its own sentence.

records.source: כִּ֤י שִׂמַּחְתַּ֣נִי יְהוָ֣ה בְּפָעֳלֶ֑ךָ בְּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖י יָדֶ֣יךָ אֲרַנֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: For you have made me glad, YHWH, by your work; at [the] works of your hands I shout for joy.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} deeds, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have filled me with joy; \q I sing out over all that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands have made.

L.5: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me glad, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work; \q at the works of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands I shout for joy.

R.5: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done make me happy. \q I sing for joy about everything {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.

decisions.choice: your work, the works of your hands: what God has made and done
decisions.reason: The words take in creation and God's acts in history, including the judgment of the wicked in verses 8-12 (90:16; 143:5).

decisions.choice: all that your hands have made (B); everything you have done (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of hands; Readable says it plainly.

records.source: מַה־גָּדְל֣וּ מַעֲשֶׂ֣יךָ יְהוָ֑ה מְ֝אֹ֗ד עָמְק֥וּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: How great are your works, YHWH! Exceedingly deep are your thoughts.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how great the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do! \q How very deep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} plans!

L.6: How great are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Exceedingly deep are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} thoughts.

R.6: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do such great things! \q Your thoughts go deeper than we can understand.

decisions.choice: deep thoughts: plans beyond human understanding
decisions.reason: God's thoughts are his purposes (33:11; 40:6), too deep for people to see to the bottom. Verse 7 says who does not understand them.

decisions.choice: go deeper than we can understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what "deep" means (m1).

records.source: אִֽישׁ־בַּ֭עַר לֹ֣א יֵדָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל לֹא־יָבִ֥ין אֶת־זֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: A stupid man not knows, and a fool not understands this:
pieces: Senseless people do not know it; \q fools cannot grasp this:

L.7: {{gender:A senseless person|A senseless man}} does not know, \q and a fool does not understand this:

R.7: Foolish people do not know this. \q People without sense cannot understand it.

decisions.choice: stupid: dull as an animal
decisions.reason: The word (ba'ar) describes a person no wiser than a beast (49:11; 73:22).

decisions.choice: this: what follows
decisions.reason: "This" points ahead to verse 8: the wicked flourish only to be destroyed.

decisions.choice: a senseless person (with "a senseless man" as the alternative at Literal); plurals at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The words describe anyone who will not understand, so Literal gives inclusive wording by default; Balanced and Readable use plurals.

records.source: בִּפְרֹ֤חַ רְשָׁעִ֨ים׀כְּמ֥וֹ עֵ֗שֶׂב וַ֭יָּצִיצוּ כָּל־פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן לְהִשָּֽׁמְדָ֥ם עֲדֵי־עַֽד׃
records.gloss: When [the] wicked sprout like grass and all [the] doers of wickedness flourish, [it is] for them to be destroyed forever.
pieces: though the wicked shoot up like green plants \q and all who do wrong are in bloom, \q it is only so that they may be destroyed for all time.

L.8: when [the] wicked sprout like grass, \q and all who do wickedness flourish, \q [it is] that they may be destroyed forever.

R.8: Wicked people may spring up like grass. \q Everyone who does evil may seem to do well. \q But they will be destroyed forever.

decisions.choice: like grass: quick to grow and quick to wither
decisions.reason: As in 37:2 and 90:5-6, grass springs up fast and dries up in a day; the righteous are like trees (verses 13-15).

decisions.choice: to be destroyed: their end
decisions.reason: The form says what their flourishing leads to: it ends in destruction for good.

records.gloss: But you [are] on high forever, YHWH.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q are enthroned on high for all time.

R.9: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q will rule from heaven forever.

decisions.choice: the center of the psalm
decisions.reason: This short line stands at the center of the psalm, with seven lines before it and seven after: the LORD above all, against the wicked who perish.

decisions.choice: on high: in the height, the place of God's throne
decisions.reason: The word (marom) is the height of heaven, where God reigns (7:8; 93:4).

decisions.choice: enthroned on high (B); rule from heaven (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being on high means (m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י הִנֵּ֪ה אֹיְבֶ֡יךָ׀יְֽהוָ֗ה כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה אֹיְבֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ יִ֝תְפָּרְד֗וּ כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: For look, your enemies, YHWH, for look, your enemies will perish; all [the] doers of wickedness will be scattered.
pieces: Look at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies are doomed; \q everyone who does evil will be driven apart.

L.10: For look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies will perish; \q all who do wickedness will be scattered.

R.10: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies will surely die. \q Everyone who does evil will be scattered.

decisions.choice: the repeated line: rising emphasis
decisions.reason: The line starts, breaks off, and starts again, adding a word each time, a pattern of Hebrew poetry (93:3; 94:3).

decisions.choice: scattered: broken up like a defeated army
decisions.reason: The verb (parad) is used of a group separated and scattered (Job 4:11).

records.source: וַתָּ֣רֶם כִּרְאֵ֣ים קַרְנִ֑י בַּ֝לֹּתִ֗י בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן רַעֲנָֽן׃
records.gloss: And you have raised like a wild ox my horn; I have been anointed with fresh oil.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me strong like a wild ox; \q fresh oil has been poured over me.

L.11: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have raised my horn like [that of] a wild ox; \q I have been anointed with fresh oil.

R.11: You have made me as strong as a wild ox. \q You have poured fresh oil on me to honor me.

decisions.choice: raised my horn: made me strong and victorious
decisions.reason: A horn is a picture of an animal's strength, and raising it means victory and honor (75:11; 89:18; 1 Samuel 2:1).

decisions.choice: I have been anointed: soaked with oil
alternatives: my old age (is) with fresh oil
decisions.reason: The verb (balal) means to moisten or mix with oil. Oil on the head was a sign of honor and joy (23:5). The ancient Greek translation reads the word as "my old age".

decisions.choice: You have poured; to honor me
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts and what the oil means (m2).

records.source: וַתַּבֵּ֥ט עֵינִ֗י בְּשׁ֫וּרָ֥י בַּקָּמִ֖ים עָלַ֥י מְרֵעִ֗ים תִּשְׁמַ֥עְנָה אָזְנָֽי׃
records.gloss: And my eye has looked on my watchers; on [those who] rise against me, evildoers, my ears have heard.
pieces: My eyes have looked in triumph on those who lay in wait for me; \q my ears have heard what became of the evildoers who rose up against me.

L.12: And my eye has looked on those who watch for me; \q of those who rise against me, evildoers, my ears have heard.

R.12: I have seen my enemies defeated. \q I have heard about the end of the evil people who attacked me.

decisions.choice: my watchers: enemies lying in wait
decisions.reason: The word (shur) is taken as the one in 5:9 and 27:11, those who watch closely for a chance to attack. A word spelled the same way means "wall".

decisions.choice: look on: look on in triumph
decisions.reason: To look on enemies is to see them defeated (54:9; 118:7). The Hebrew does not say what was seen or heard; the sense is their downfall.

decisions.choice: in triumph, what became of (B); defeated, the end of (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was seen and heard (m2).

records.source: צַ֭דִּיק כַּתָּמָ֣ר יִפְרָ֑ח כְּאֶ֖רֶז בַּלְּבָנ֣וֹן יִשְׂגֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] righteous like the palm tree will flourish; like a cedar in Lebanon he will grow.
pieces: The righteous will thrive like the palm tree \q and rise tall as a cedar on Lebanon.

L.13: [The] righteous like the palm tree will flourish; \q like a cedar in Lebanon {{gender:they|he}} will grow.

R.13: People who do what is right will grow strong like palm trees. \q They will grow tall like the cedar trees in Lebanon.

decisions.choice: palm and cedar: green, tall and long-lived
decisions.reason: The date palm stays green in dry land and bears fruit for many years; the cedars of Lebanon were the tallest and strongest trees known (Isaiah 2:13; Ezekiel 31:3). They stand against the grass of verse 8.

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who live rightly before God
decisions.reason: The word (tsaddiq) is singular, standing for every such person (1:6).

decisions.choice: they (with "he" as the alternative at Literal)
decisions.reason: "The righteous" stands for anyone who lives this way (m2), so Literal gives "they" by default; Balanced and Readable need no pronoun or use the plural.

records.source: שְׁ֭תוּלִים בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בְּחַצְר֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣ינוּ יַפְרִֽיחוּ׃
records.gloss: Planted in [the] house of YHWH, in [the] courts of our God they will flourish.
pieces: Rooted in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house, \q they will bloom in the courtyards of our God.

L.14: Planted in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q in the courts of our God they will flourish.

R.14: They are like trees planted at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q They grow strong in the courtyards of our God's temple.

decisions.choice: planted in the house of the LORD: living near God
decisions.reason: Trees in the temple courts are a picture of those who live close to God and draw life from him (52:10; 1:3).

decisions.choice: They are like trees
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison clear.

records.source: ע֭וֹד יְנוּב֣וּן בְּשֵׂיבָ֑ה דְּשֵׁנִ֖ים וְרַֽעֲנַנִּ֣ים יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Still they will bear fruit in old age; full of sap and fresh they will be,
pieces: Even when they are old they will still bear fruit; \q they will stay rich with sap and green,

L.15: Still they will bear fruit in old age; \q full of sap and fresh they will be,

R.15: Even when they are old, they will still produce fruit. \q They will stay healthy and strong.

decisions.choice: full of sap and fresh: healthy and vigorous
decisions.reason: The first word (dashen) means fat, rich, and so thriving; the second (ra'anan) is green and fresh, the word used of the oil in verse 11.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The thought continues in verse 16, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: healthy and strong
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: לְ֭הַגִּיד כִּֽי־יָשָׁ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה צ֝וּרִ֗י וְֽלֹא־עַוְלָ֥תָה בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: to declare that upright [is] YHWH, my rock, and there is no injustice in him.
pieces: bearing witness that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is just: \q my rock, in whom nothing is crooked.

L.16: to declare that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] upright — \q my rock, and there is no injustice in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.16: Their lives will show that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is fair. \q He is my rock, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never does anything wrong.

decisions.choice: upright, rock, no injustice: the song of Moses
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 32:4 uses the same words of God: "the Rock ... a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he".

decisions.choice: my rock: a safe, unshakable place
decisions.reason: As in 18:3, a rock is a place of safety and strength.

decisions.choice: Their lives will show
decisions.reason: Readable says how the flourishing righteous declare it: by what their lives show.
